extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, containing erroneous and successful manipulation trajectories with multi-dimensional QA annotations for task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu; Minghao Ye; Zewei Ye; Ruihan Tao; Shuo Yang; Bo Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in both simulation and real-world settings. In simulation, the authors collected data for 14 robotic tasks in ManiSkill, augmented with YCB objects and ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR scenes. They defined expert policies and then injected erroneous code snippets at selected substages to generate failure trajectories, recording each failure video with a textual description. In the real world, they collected data for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm, also pairing each video with a textual description. They additionally collected successful trajectories to reduce overfitting to failure patterns.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper states that motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions. The authors manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of robot manipulation videos and corresponding textual descriptions from simulation and real-world executions. Simulation data came from ManiSkill with YCB objects and ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR scenes; real-world data came from teleoperated SO-100 robotic arm tasks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Failure trajectories were created by replacing the original expert policy with erroneous code snippets at selected substages to induce task failure. The dataset also introduced variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints to increase visual diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors manually cleaned the collected simulation data because motion planning sometimes failed and produced trajectories inconsistent with the textual descriptions; they retained approximately 75% of the collected data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw videos were annotated into video-based QA samples for eight question types. For each question type, five templates were provided. Reference answers for task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating were directly extracted from the textual descriptions. For failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction, GPT-4o generated reference answers using both the video and textual description, and all GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: GPT-4o-generated annotations for failure explanation and correction were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 question-answer pairs per video sample across eight question types
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and model are intended to improve robotic failure handling and recovery, enabling more robust and transparent deployment of vision-language models in challenging robotic manipulation scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note a risk of models overfitting to failure patterns and mitigate this by collecting successful trajectories in addition to failure trajectories.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of RoboFAC correction suggestions into VLA-controlled robotic systems is not yet seamless. The work applies the model exclusively to VLA models, and success rates are still limited partly because the VLA model has limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used to train and evaluate models for robotic failure video understanding, including task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction. The authors construct training and testing splits from RoboFAC data, using 60K simulated QA pairs for training and the remaining simulated and real-world QA pairs for evaluation.
